sources.title: Michael W. Davis, The Geometry and Topology of Coxeter Groups (Princeton University Press, 2008; author's complete institutional PDF)
sources.locator: S4.2, printed pp. 45-47; S4.8, printed pp. 54-57; S4.9, printed pp. 57-59; Appendix D.1, printed pp. 439-442; Appendix D.2, printed pp. 442-443; read in the extracted full text of the author-hosted PDF; figures and exercises excluded

contents.name: S4.2, Lemma 4.2.1: the Cayley-graph wall sets R(u,v), their conjugation and symmetric-difference identities, Card R(1,u) = l(u) and the word metric as a wall count
contents.reason: This pair proves the chamber-descent correspondence from the half-space induction (Pn),(Qn) instead of by Cayley-graph wall counting, so the wall-count machinery has no consumer here; the geometric separation statement itself is built as part (4) of the rank-two/chamber lemma.

contents.name: S4.2, Lemma 4.2.2: a reflection r separates 1 from w if and only if l(w) > l(rw), proved by reflecting the edge path and deleting one letter
S4.8, Property (P) and Remark 4.8.1: prefundamental vertex sets, and (P) implies B = intersection of the Bs is prefundamental
S4.8, Remark 4.8.2 and Condition (C'): the warning that (P) alone does not make a pre-Coxeter system a Coxeter system
contents.reason: A warning about pre-Coxeter systems; this pair works inside a fixed presented Coxeter system and does not characterise Coxeter systems from (P), so no local item consumes the remark.

contents.name: S4.8, Lemma 4.8.3 (Tits): the simultaneous assertions (Pn) and (Qn), the trivial base cases, and the two implication proofs ((Pn),(Qn)) => (Pn+1) and ((Pn+1),(Qn)) => (Qn+1)
S4.9, Theorem 4.9.2 and Complement 4.9.3: the rank-two case analysis for half-spaces As cap At, with the affine-line picture for m = infinity and the Euclidean-sector picture for m < infinity
S4.9, proof of Theorem 4.9.2: reflection subgroups W' generated by a set X of reflections, chambers of W' on the Cayley graph, and property (P) for (W', S'(D))
contents.reason: Reflection subgroups of Coxeter systems are outside this pair's scope; the run's design scaffolds no reflection-subgroup item, and only Complement 4.9.3's rank-two analysis is consumed here.

contents.name: Appendix D.1, Theorem D.1.1: if w C-dot intersects C-dot then w = 1, together with its proof from Lemma 4.8.3
Appendix D.1, Corollary D.1.2: faithfulness of the canonical representation rho (and of rho*), and Corollary D.1.3: discreteness of rho(W)
Appendix D.1, Corollary D.1.3 second clause and Corollary D.1.4: discreteness of rho*(W), and virtual torsion-freeness via Selberg's lemma
contents.reason: Only discreteness/isolation of the canonical representation is used by thm-cg-finite-type-positive-definite-criterion on the finite-classification page. The grouped virtual torsion-freeness clause requires Selberg and is neither promised nor consumed anywhere in the approved 32-pair scope.

contents.name: Appendix D.1, Lemma D.1.5: v(As cap At) is contained in As or in sAs, and in the second case l(sv) = l(v) - 1, with the m = infinity affine-line proof and the m < infinity positive-definite-plane proof
Appendix D.1, the dual reflection formula (D.1) and the description of C as a simplicial cone with interior defined by strict inequalities
Appendix D.2, Examples D.2.1 and Lemmas D.2.2-D.2.3: the Tits cone U as the union of the chambers, the Cayley-graph embedding w -> wx, and the finiteness criterion via -C-dot contained in U
contents.reason: The Tits cone, its interior, the boundary comparison and the finiteness criterion are the subject of the Tits-cones pair of this run, which declares the canonical-roots pair as its prerequisite; no item of this pair may claim them.

contents.name: Appendix D.2, the mirror structure of C: faces CT, relative interiors C-dot-T, the open part C-f = union of C-dot-T over spherical T, and the CW comparison U vs I
contents.reason: The chamber face strata and spherical-stabilizer interior criterion are proved at thm-cg-dual-chamber-intersections-and-point-stabilizers and thm-cg-tits-cone-interior-and-local-finiteness on batch9. The grouped universal basic-construction/CW comparison of U with I is not a promised theorem of these Tits-cone items.

sources.title: Anders Bjorner and Francesco Brenti, Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups (Graduate Texts in Mathematics 231, Springer 2005; author-hosted full PDF)
sources.locator: S1.3, printed pp. 11-13; S1.4, printed pp. 15-18; S4.2, printed pp. 93-97; S4.4, printed pp. 101-105; S4.5, printed p. 105 (statement only); read in the extracted full text; exercises excluded

contents.name: S1.3, (1.7)-(1.14) and (1.15)-(1.18): the reflection set T, prefix reflections T(s), the count n(s;t), the sign eta(s;t) and the permutation action pi_s on T x {+1,-1}
S1.3, Theorem 1.3.2: the pi-action extends uniquely to an injective homomorphism W -> S(T x {+1,-1}), and pi_t(t,eps) = (t,-eps)
contents.reason: The signed action and its faithfulness are built in this run by that pair's exchange/faithfulness theorem (batch 2), which this pair consumes through it; restating it here would duplicate the supplier.

contents.name: S1.4, Proposition 1.4.2: parity and epsilon(w) = (-1)^l(w), l(sw) = l(w) +/- 1, l(w^-1) = l(w), and the triangle inequalities for l
S1.4, Theorem 1.4.3 (Strong Exchange): if l(tw) < l(w) then tw = s_1 ... shat_i ... s_k, proved through the equivalence with eta(w;t) = -1
S1.4, Corollary 1.4.4: the equivalences T_L(w) = {t : l(tw) < l(w)} = {prefix reflections}, with uniquely determined index i
S1.4, Corollary 1.4.5: Card T_L(w) = l(w)
S1.4, Corollary 1.4.6: s is in D_L(w) iff some reduced expression for w begins with s (right form by symmetry)
contents.reason: The descent-letter characterisation is the exchange theorem's first-letter clause, built in this run on that pair (batch 2); this pair consumes only the length change l(ws) = l(w) +/- 1.

contents.name: S1.4, Proposition 1.4.7 and Corollary 1.4.8: the deletion property, the reduced-subword characterisation, and independence of the letter set of a reduced expression
contents.reason: Deletion, subword reduction and support are built in this run on that pair (batch 2) and on the parabolic pair; this pair uses them only through those suppliers' statements.

contents.name: S4.2, Proposition 4.2.1, Theorem 4.2.2 and Proposition 4.2.3: sigma_s are involutions with sigma_s sigma_s' of order m(s,s'), the homomorphism sigma: W -> GL(V) and contragredience of sigma and sigma*
contents.reason: The representation, its descent and the exact rank-two orders are built in this run on that pair (batch 4) as its canonical-form and reflection-order items; this pair consumes them there, with the real Coxeter form rather than the weights k_{s,s'}/2 used here.

contents.name: S4.2, Lemma 4.2.4: for j < m(s,s') the alternating prefix (...s'ss')_j applied to alpha_s is c alpha_s + d alpha_{s'} with c,d >= 0
S4.2, Proposition 4.2.5: l(ws) > l(w) implies w(alpha_s) > 0, and l(ws) < l(w) implies w(alpha_s) < 0
S4.2, Corollary 4.2.6: for p in the positive orthant, D_L(u) = {s : <u(p),alpha_s> < 0}, and u(p) <> v(p) for u <> v
S4.2, Theorem 4.2.7: the geometric representation sigma and its contragredient sigma* are injective
S4.2, proof of Proposition 4.2.5: invocation of the canonical parabolic decomposition w = w^J w_J (Proposition 2.4.4)
contents.reason: The canonical decomposition and length additivity are built in this run as the parabolic minimal-representative theorem on that pair (batch 2), which this pair uses directly for its own (Q_n) induction.

contents.name: S4.4, Definition 4.4.1 with (4.24)-(4.27): the root system Phi = {w(alpha_s)}, positive and negative roots with Phi = Phi+ disjoint-union Phi-, Phi- = -Phi+, and unit B-norm of roots
S4.4, (4.25): w(alpha_s) is in Phi+ if and only if l(ws) > l(w)
S4.4, Lemma 4.4.3: the simple reflection s permutes Phi+ minus {alpha_s}
S4.4, (4.28) and Proposition 4.4.4: N(w) = {beta in Phi+ : w(beta) in Phi-} and l(w) = Card N(w), by induction over a right multiplication
S4.4, (4.29)-(4.32) and Proposition 4.4.5: t_gamma = wsw^-1 for gamma = w(alpha_s), the bijection Phi+ -> T and w t_gamma w^-1 = t_{w(gamma)}
S4.4, Proposition 4.4.6: w(gamma) in Phi- if and only if l(w t_gamma) < l(w)
S4.5, Lemma 4.5.1: for p in C the stabiliser in W is the parabolic W_J with J = {s : <p,alpha_s> = 0}
contents.reason: Stabilisers of points of the chamber are the subject of the Tits-cones pair, which declares this pair as its prerequisite; this pair deliberately makes no stabiliser claim.
